snapshot: WHO Western Pacific Region. Singapore became a super-aged society in 2026, with 21% or more of residents aged 65 and above, and health policy is built around prevention (Healthier SG), precision medicine and financing for an ageing population.

agenda.title: Healthier SG and preventive care
agenda.text: Healthier SG, the national programme that moves care from treating illness to staying healthy, has enrolled close to 60% of eligible residents aged 40 and above with a regular family doctor. Next steps are an AI tool that flags people with a high chance of developing diabetes or high cholesterol (rolling out to doctors from 2027) and a proof of concept pairing traditional Chinese medicine practitioners with family doctors, targeted for the first half of 2027.

src.t: Ministry of Health (Committee of Supply, 5 March 2026)

agenda.title: Precision medicine and genomics
agenda.text: The National Precision Medicine Programme has sequenced the whole genome of more than 100,000 residents, and its next phase aims to recruit 450,000 more. Subsidised genetic testing for hereditary breast and ovarian cancer starts in December 2026. Partnerships with Amazon Web Services and Temus are meant to build the genomic data infrastructure, and a law on the use of genetic information in insurance and employment has been through public consultation.

src.t: Ministry of Health (Committee of Supply, 5 March 2026)

agenda.title: Financing healthcare for an ageing population
agenda.text: The government health budget is about 2.7% of GDP and is expected to reach about 3.5% by 2030, from roughly S$22.5 billion this year to about S$30 billion. From January 2027 the MediSave500/700 scheme becomes the MediSave Chronic and Preventive Care Scheme with higher annual withdrawal limits (S$700 and S$1,000), benefiting more than 910,000 patients. 2,800 more public acute and community hospital beds are planned for 2025 to 2030.

src.t: Ministry of Health (Committee of Supply, 5 March 2026)

agenda.title: Vigilance on Ebola at the border
agenda.text: On 19 May 2026 the Communicable Diseases Agency stepped up precautions over the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda: health advisories at all points of entry, 21 days of self-monitoring for returning travellers, and a reminder to doctors to watch for compatible symptoms. That release reported no case in Singapore.
